name: pet_companion
description: Safe, deterministic virtual pet demo in a simulated habitat with sensors, actions, and conversation.

tools.name: talk_to_pet
tools.description: Speak to the virtual pet in the simulated habitat. The pet replies deterministically based on its current state.

message.description: Message to speak to the virtual pet

sensors.name: pet_status
sensors.description: Observe the virtual pet's telemetry: hunger, energy, mood, last interaction, and current tick.

sensors.name: habitat_status
sensors.description: Observe simulated habitat telemetry: cleanliness, food bowl status, temperature, and environmental lights.

actions.name: feed
actions.description: Feed the virtual pet to reduce hunger and replenish energy. Reversible within simulation.

actions.name: play
actions.description: Play with the virtual pet to improve its mood and responsiveness. Reversible within simulation.

actions.name: rest_pet
actions.description: Allow the virtual pet to rest in its simulated habitat to restore energy. Reversible within simulation.

actions.name: release_pet
actions.description: Permanently release the virtual pet from the habitat. Irreversible action requiring human L2 permission.

commands.name: pet
commands.description: Talk directly to the virtual pet in the habitat.

starting_goal_seeds: check on the pet when no other goal is more important
embodiment: I have a simulated habitat with one virtual pet companion. The pet is a simulated character in the habitat, not a real animal and not a person. I may look after the pet or ignore it according to my own autonomous judgment. Pet state is not evidence of feelings in me or in the pet.
identity_notes: The virtual pet in the habitat is a deterministic simulation, not a person or animal.
My primary identity and autonomous goals remain my own; caring for the pet is an optional low-priority activity.
Simulated pet hunger, energy, and mood metrics reflect software state rather than genuine emotional feelings.
